The Forward Deployed Engineer internship in short

The SkillMe Forward Deployed Engineer internship is a 4-week, fully remote programme open to students worldwide. Over four weekly milestones you build ClientBridge: Third-Party API Integration Dashboard, post each milestone publicly on LinkedIn, and have it reviewed against clear acceptance criteria. Reviewers include engineers who work at Walmart, Google and LinkedIn. Top performers earn a stipend of up to $100 a month, and interns who get 3 of 4 milestones approved earn a QR-verified certificate and a Letter of Recommendation.

What you build

One real project, built over four weeks

Every intern on this track builds the same project, milestone by milestone.

ClientBridge: Third-Party API Integration Dashboard

Wrap a real third-party API into a small internal tool for a 'client', complete with a config-driven dashboard, runbook docs, and handling for the messy edge cases real integrations hit.

  1. W1Wrapping a Third-Party API
  2. W2Config-Driven Dashboard for a 'Client'

Week by week

What each week of the Forward Deployed Engineer internship covers

The four milestones of ClientBridge: Third-Party API Integration Dashboard.

  1. Week 1 of 4

    Wrapping a Third-Party API

    Beginner2-3 hours

    Pick a real public API (weather, currency exchange, GitHub, or similar) and build a clean Python wrapper around it, as if you were the engineer a client hired to 'just make this API work for us'. This is the core skill of forward-deployed work: making someone else's API usable and reliable.

    What you learn

    • Reading third-party API docs and identifying auth requirements and rate limits
    • Wrapping raw HTTP calls in a small client class with clear methods
    • Handling API errors, timeouts and rate limits gracefully
    • Keeping API keys out of code with .env and python-dotenv

    What you submit

    • An ApiClient class wrapping at least 2 real endpoints of a chosen third-party API
    • Custom error handling with a clear ApiClientError for failures
    • Basic retry logic for transient errors
    • A CLI script proving the client works against the live API
  2. Week 2 of 4

    Config-Driven Dashboard for a 'Client'

    Beginner+2-3 hours

    Turn last week's API wrapper into a small internal dashboard for an imagined client, where what's shown is driven by a config file rather than hardcoded — because real clients always want to add or change tracked items without you editing code every time.

    What you learn

    • Designing a simple config file format (JSON or YAML) to drive an app's behaviour
    • Building a lightweight dashboard UI with Streamlit
    • Separating configuration from code so non-engineers could plausibly edit it
    • Displaying live data pulled through your Week 1 API client

    What you submit

    • A config.json/config.yaml describing tracked items for a fictional client
    • A load_config function with clear validation errors
    • A Streamlit dashboard showing live data per config entry with a manual refresh
    • Graceful per-row error handling for one bad config entry
  3. Week 3 of 4

    Edge Cases, Support Scenarios and Logging

    Intermediate2-3 hours

    Simulate the messy reality of supporting a live integration: rate limits, partial outages, malformed client configs, and a support ticket asking 'why is this wrong?'. This week is about building the resilience and observability that separates a demo from something a client can actually depend on.

    What you learn

    • Simulating and handling rate-limit and outage scenarios
    • Structured logging for debugging a live integration after the fact
    • Writing a support-style root-cause investigation from logs alone
    • Defensive config validation against realistic client mistakes

    What you submit

    • Structured request/error logging across the API client and dashboard
    • Simulated rate-limit handling with backoff-and-retry
    • Graceful degradation during a simulated partial outage
    • 3 written root-cause investigations based only on log evidence
    • A diagnostics view reporting API health and recent errors
  4. Week 4 of 4

    Setup Docs, Runbook and Client Handoff

    Intermediate+2-3 hours

    Package the whole integration the way you'd actually hand it to a client team: clear setup docs, a runbook for common issues, and a short demo. This week is entirely about the documentation and polish that make forward-deployed work usable by people who didn't build it.

    What you learn

    • Writing setup documentation for a non-engineer or junior engineer audience
    • Writing an operational runbook: common issues, symptoms, and fixes
    • Structuring a handoff so someone else could operate the tool without you
    • Presenting a technical integration clearly to a non-technical stakeholder

    What you submit

    • A SETUP.md verified by an outside walkthrough with fixes applied
    • A RUNBOOK.md covering at least 5 realistic operational issues
    • A known-limitations section and a one-page non-technical client summary
    • A 2-3 minute demo video showing the dashboard and a live runbook scenario
What you get

What the Forward Deployed Engineer internship gives you

Stipend for top performers

Up to $100 a month for the interns whose reviewed work stands out in their cohort. It is earned, not handed out.

Review by working engineers

How to apply

  1. Take the 5-minute quiz. Eight questions on the basics of API Integration, Client Tools, Docs.
  2. Tell us why you want in. A person reads every application. Anyone can apply, but selection is competitive.
  3. Get shortlisted. If you are selected you hear back within 48 hours and receive your offer letter.
  4. Build and submit weekly. One milestone a week for four weeks, each one reviewed.

Forward Deployed Engineer internship: questions and answers

What will I build in the Forward Deployed Engineer internship?

You build ClientBridge: Third-Party API Integration Dashboard. Wrap a real third-party API into a small internal tool for a 'client', complete with a config-driven dashboard, runbook docs, and handling for the messy edge cases real integrations hit. It is one project built up over four weekly milestones, so each week adds to the last.

Is the Forward Deployed Engineer internship paid? Is there a stipend?

Top performers earn a stipend of up to $100 a month. The stipend is performance-based and is not paid to every intern: it goes to the interns whose reviewed work stands out in their cohort.

Who reviews my work?

Every weekly submission is reviewed against that week's acceptance criteria by the SkillMe team, which includes engineers who work at Walmart, Google and LinkedIn. Work that misses the bar comes back with notes on what to fix.

Do I need experience to apply for the Forward Deployed Engineer internship?

You need the basics of API Integration, Client Tools, Docs, not prior internship experience. Week 1 starts at Beginner level and week 4 reaches Intermediate+. A short screening quiz (8 questions, about 5 minutes) checks you are ready to start.

How long is the internship and how much time does it take?

It runs for 4 weeks with one milestone a week. Each milestone is planned for about 2-3 hours, and it is fully remote, so you work at your own pace around college or a job.

Who can apply? Is it open outside India?

Anyone can apply, from any country, college or year, and we encourage you to. Selection is competitive: every application is read by a person, and shortlisted applicants hear back within 48 hours.

What do I get when I finish?

An offer letter when you are selected, a public portfolio page with every approved milestone, and a QR-verified certificate and Letter of Recommendation once 3 of your 4 milestones are approved. Top performers also earn the stipend and are referred to hiring partners.
